references.text: The continuation of the story where Gideon and his men use horns, jars, and torches in the attack against the Midianites.
God chooses the 300 men that Gideon will use, mentioned here as they are divided into three groups.
Moses used the horn (shofar) as a signal in the wilderness, similar to the use of horns as signaling tools.
Joshua's conquest of Jericho also involved horns (shofar) as an instrument in God's strategy for victory.
Paul writes that we have this treasure in jars of clay, an image reminiscent of the empty jars that hid the light.
Jesus speaks about not hiding the light under a jar but setting it out - a similar image with light and a jar.
